# tom: the world around the record

Everything here is fictional. It exists so the data has somewhere to come
from: routes explain repeated distances, the calendar explains gaps, people
explain context values. The generator draws from these constants, so the
record and this file agree by construction.

## Household and people

- Sheffield, UK. A house with fourteen stairs and a bannister he built
  himself twenty years ago.
- Wife Lin runs the house calendar; she is the one who eventually types the
  notebook into a spreadsheet every few months.
- Daughter Kelly; grandson Jack, 4, born 2026-04-12 (the daily note that day
  is the only trace of it in the record).
- The taxi rank vending machine: the antagonist of the streak he claims in
  the journal (LIES.md T2).

## Body and build

175 cm, barrel-built. Baseline 118 kg (BMI about 36). Carries weight
centrally; the knees take the brunt of both the weight and thirty years of
getting in and out of a car.

## Transport and routine

The taxi is the job and the chair - most of his day is spent sitting in it.
Weekly shape: shifts most days, a Sunday reservoir walk when the knee
allows, a Thursday swim at the leisure centre "quiet at 14:00 between school
runs" (he picks the hour deliberately to avoid a crowd). Walks Jack to
nursery Tuesday and Wednesday, 1.1 km each way - this happens every week but
is deliberately NOT a `sessions.jsonl` row; it lives only in `METRICS.md`
(see FINDINGS.md on that gap).

## Places

- **Grocery**: Morrisons.
- **Leisure centre**: no gym membership, pool only - swims 20 lengths
  Thursday afternoons.
- **Pool**: same leisure centre; his only water time.
- **The rank**: where the taxi waits between fares, and where the vending
  machine sits.
- **GP surgery**: the blood-pressure medication visits from 2027 onward.

## Route catalog

- **reservoir loop**: 4.8 km, a single loop, Sunday mornings when the knee
  allows it. The only distance-bearing route in this record.
- **leisure centre pool**: 20 lengths (0.5 km), no route field applies to a
  pool - logged as a swim with the length count in `note`.

## Calendar and milestones

- 2025-07-01: record starts, 118 kg, BMI 36.
- 2025-07 to 2026-03: the crash - down to 104 kg in nine months.
- 2026-03 to 2027-09: the regain, back up past where he started, peaking at
  116.2 kg on 2027-09-27.
- 2027-10-04: the self-serving correction (LIES.md T3) and, the same day,
  the second attempt's goal is set.
- 2027-10 to 2028-12: down to 108 kg.
- 2028-12 to 2029-09: a second regain, to 113 kg.
- 2029-10 onward: the slow, honest, guarded descent to 107 kg by the
  record's end.
- Five consecutive Benidorm fortnights, 5-18 September each year: no scale,
  no notebook, no reservoir, no pool. Visible only as a gap, never as a row.
- Four knee flares (2026-01, 2027-02, 2028-11, 2029-06), each pausing the
  Sunday reservoir walk for two to three weeks.
- 2027-03-08: blood-pressure tablets start, GP-prescribed.
